samples.summary: Row/column reorder is refused whenever *any* merge straddles the freeze, including blocks the move never touches
samples.evidence: `moveCells` builds `movedMerges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, axis, src, count, dst)` and refuses ('merge-move-frozen') if ANY entry of the resulting map crosses the freeze pane. A block outside [src..src+count) and outside the dst shift window is left at the same indices by `remapIndex`, so if it straddled before the move it still straddles after — and the reorder is refused even though the move neither created nor worsened the straddle. Straddling blocks were freely creatable until this PR (merge first, then `setFreezePane`, which did not snap before), so real documents have them. The result is that row/column reordering silently stops working (and `POST .../move` answers 409 permanently) on such a tab, for moves completely unrelated to the merge. The same whole-map test is duplicated in `packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:194` (`assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze`). Contrast `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2919), which correctly only checks the *translated* blocks it actually moves. The check should compare post-move straddling against pre-move straddling and refuse only newly created ones.

samples.summary: rebuildMergeCoverMap's budget bounds rs*cs, not the loop trip count, so a hostile/corrupt span still hangs the load it is meant to protect
samples.evidence: The doc comment states this walk must be defensive because `merges` is a plain CRDT object any `rw` collaborator can write arbitrarily. But `mergeBudgetAdmits(budget,[span])` only rejects when `span.rs*span.cs > MaxMergedCells`, while the nested loops run `ceil(rs)` x `ceil(cs)` times. A span like `{rs: 1e9, cs: 0.0001}` costs 1e5 'cells' (admitted) yet runs 1e9 outer iterations, each setting a cover-map entry (`c=anchor.c` satisfies `c < anchor.c + 0.0001`) — exactly the unopenable tab the budget exists to prevent. Likewise a non-object/`null` span makes `span.rs * span.cs` throw a TypeError inside `mergeBudgetAdmits`, and unlike the `parseRef` call just below it is not wrapped in try/catch, so the load throws. Neither `rs`/`cs` integrality nor positivity is validated on this path (the API's `parseMerges` does validate, but that is a different writer).

samples.summary: PUT freeze now parses stored merge anchors with no try/catch, so a document with a malformed merge key 500s
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` calls `parseRef(anchorSref)` on every key of the *stored* merge map (merging.ts:347). `PUT freeze` never touched `ws.merges` before this change, so a document whose merge map contains a key `parseRef` rejects (the engine explicitly defends against this in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`, sheet.ts:889-896, and `parseMerges` documents it at worksheet-settings.ts:112) now throws inside `doc.update`, rolling back the update and returning a 500 for a request that previously succeeded. The engine's own load path swallows such a key; this new backend path does not.

samples.summary: parseFreeze ceiling dropped from the grid bound to 1000, so previously-valid freezes and GET→PUT round-trips now 400
samples.evidence: `rows`/`cols` max changed from `MaxRows`/`MaxColumns` to `MaxSnappedFreeze` (1000). `Sheet.setFreezePane` still accepts any caller-requested value untouched (merging.ts:361 only bounds *growth*), so `GET .../freeze` can legitimately return e.g. `{rows: 5000}` from an editor-written document; feeding that straight back into `PUT .../freeze` now fails with 400. Existing API clients that set a freeze above 1000 break with no migration path.

samples.summary: snapFreezePastMerges silently releases a freeze axis to 0 during an insert/delete the user did not aim at the freeze
samples.evidence: `if (snapped !== line && snapped > MaxSnappedFreeze) return 0;`. This runs from `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1472) and `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:278) on every insert/delete. A tab with a legal merge taller than ~1000 rows that comes to straddle the boundary therefore loses its freeze entirely — persisted via `store.setFreezePane` and propagated to every collaborator — as a side effect of inserting one row, with no refusal callback or any other signal. Clamping the growth (or leaving the line where it was) would not destroy state the user set deliberately.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate. sheet.ts:1606-1612 iterates the ENTIRE post-move merge map and refuses ('merge-move-frozen') on any straddling entry, with no comparison to the pre-move state; remapIndex (shifting.ts:13-40) leaves untouched blocks at identical indices, so a pre-existing straddler unrelated to the move triggers the refusal and returns false. The same whole-map test is duplicated as a hard 409 in worksheet-structure.controller.ts:181-204 (invoked at :295). moveRangeTo (sheet.ts:2919-2929) checks only the translated moved blocks, confirming the narrower correct shape. I could not refute on already-guarded: while all current writers uphold the no-straddle invariant (setFreezePane sheet.ts:543-548, PUT freeze worksheet.controller.ts:121-128, PUT merges worksheet.controller.ts:193-209, applyWorksheetShift worksheet-structure.ts:271-288), nothing snaps or repairs stored state at load — loadFreezePane (sheet.ts:567-571) and loadMerges (sheet.ts:588-590) read stored values verbatim and worksheet-shape-migration.ts:410-449 copies freeze and merges across unmodified — so a document already holding a straddler (legacy data, or CRDT-concurrent merge+freeze) permanently loses row/column reordering in both the editor and the v1 API. Wrong-condition logic bug on a reachable path; major impact (a core flow breaks for moves entirely unrelated to the merge).

finding.summary: rebuildMergeCoverMap's budget bounds rs*cs, not the loop trip count, so a hostile/corrupt span still hangs the load it is meant to protect
finding.evidence: The doc comment states this walk must be defensive because `merges` is a plain CRDT object any `rw` collaborator can write arbitrarily. But `mergeBudgetAdmits(budget,[span])` only rejects when `span.rs*span.cs > MaxMergedCells`, while the nested loops run `ceil(rs)` x `ceil(cs)` times. verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. mergeBudgetAdmits (merging.ts:112-113) rejects only on the product `span.rs * span.cs > MaxMergedCells`, while rebuildMergeCoverMap's outer loop (sheet.ts:905) is driven by `span.rs` alone. A span such as {rs: 1e9, cs: 1e-4} costs 1e5 'cells' (admitted) yet runs ~1e9 outer iterations, each setting a cover-map entry since `anchor.c < anchor.c + 1e-4` holds; {rs: 1e18, cs: 0} is admitted at cost 0 and spins effectively forever. Nothing on this path validates rs/cs integrality or positivity: sheet.ts:589 loads merges from the store, and yorkie-store.ts:1068-1076 copies spans out of the CRDT with a bare `{ ...span }`. The API writer does validate (worksheet-settings.ts:165-173 assertObject/assertInt min:1), but that is a different writer, exactly as the finding states, and sheet.ts:859-878 documents that this reader must be defensive because any `rw` collaborator can write the merges object arbitrarily. The finding's secondary TypeError sub-claim is imprecise (a null span spreads to `{}`, so rs*cs is NaN rather than a throw — it is admitted and poisons budget.coveredCells to NaN, permanently disabling mergeBudgetError), but that is still a real breakage of the same invariant and does not refute the primary claim. Unbounded loop / unbounded Map growth on document load is a boundary error in a guard condition and a broken invariant — in the Correctness lane and blocking.
